solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alarm rattles building

indicators.note: building here means constructing something new, so the letters of rattles are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A building is shaking so much that its occupants become frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to frighten them suddenly, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Wild capers may get you into one

definitions.text: Wild capers may get you into one

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of capers run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting up to wild antics can land you in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a predicament or awkward fix, the kind of trouble wild antics cause.

clue.text: Sailor is married to Elizabeth — a superior lady

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common term for a sailor
Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A sailor's wife Elizabeth is a woman of high standing.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent is a Mother Superior, a woman superior in rank.

clue.text: In fact, solo composition is a method of teaching music

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the opening words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solo piece is said to be a way of teaching music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight-singing system using doh, ray, me syllables, used for teaching singing.

clue.text: One playing minor part in run

definitions.meaning: a film actor in a non-speaking crowd role
in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.definitionFit: A walk-on actor is called this, as is a bye or wide added to a cricket score.

clue.text: It may lead to quick duck for any batsman

definitions.text: It may lead to quick duck for any batsman

parts.words: It may lead to quick duck for any batsman
parts.note: a short-pitched cricket delivery rearing at the head makes the batsman duck down fast; a duck is also a score of nought

explanation.surface: A cricket ball that makes any batsman get out cheaply for nought.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, but here the batsman ducks his head. The ball rears up at head height after pitching short.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a fast short-pitched ball that rises sharply at the batsman's head.

clue.text: Were debts spread out? Yes!

indicators.note: spread out means scattered, so the letters of the first two words are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether repayments were spread over time, and is told they were.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word meaning scattered over, the past tense of strewing things about.

clue.text: State university with rising capital investment

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the piece is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a hat is something invested in, or put on, the head, the capital

explanation.surface: A state college with investment money growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means head, and to invest once meant to clothe, so a hat is what the head wears.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, in the Rocky Mountain west.

clue.text: New couples finally succeeded to become big shots

indicators.note: finally places the succeeded abbreviation at the very end
new signals that the letters of couples are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Newly-wed pairs eventually become important people.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots in films or photography taken at close range make the subject appear big.

clue.text: Arrested, perhaps, and recovered tyres

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of arrested may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone stopped by police, possibly, with retreaded wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Old tyres given a new tread, so recovered in the sense of covered again.

clue.text: Backing writer or flier

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the two pieces before the definition are read from right to left

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone supports either an author or an aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is anything that flies, and this common garden songbird is one.

clue.text: Throw a fight and spend night worrying?

parts.note: to toss is to throw
taken as written
a bout is a boxing contest

explanation.surface: A boxer who has thrown a fight lies awake that night worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious in bed turns restlessly from side to side all night, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Carriers available for small charges

parts.note: small charges are little children in someone's care, and the carriers are wheeled seats for them

explanation.surface: Delivery firms offer cheap rates for low fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding wheeled seats for toddlers carry children, who are the small charges of a parent.

clue.text: Such wolves are no longer

definitions.meaning: werewolves: the prefix attached to wolves names men who turn into them
the past tense of are, so what are no longer is what once ...

explanation.definitionFit: It is the prefix of the mythical werewolf and also the past plural of the verb be.

clue.text: Little may be seen through it

definitions.text: Little may be seen through it

parts.words: Little may be seen through it
parts.note: it seems to say not much is visible, but it means tiny things become visible

explanation.surface: A window so dirty that hardly anything can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory instrument with lenses that magnifies tiny objects for viewing.

clue.text: Flogged by a stock-holder?

parts.note: a stock-holder is read as a rider holding a whip with a stock, or handle, rather than an investor

explanation.surface: A shareholder sold off assets, or was punished by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten with a riding whip, whose handle is called its stock, means being thrashed.

clue.text: They are known to go round with crooks

definitions.text: They are known to go round with crooks

parts.words: They are known to go round with crooks
parts.note: crooks are hooked staffs carried by flock-keepers, not criminals

explanation.surface: People with a reputation for keeping bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers of flocks traditionally carry hooked staffs called crooks.

clue.text: Asked for and attracted interest

definitions.meaning: was attractive or pleasing to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both making an earnest request and being attractive to people.

clue.text: He does his writing in bars

definitions.text: He does his writing in bars

parts.words: He does his writing in bars
parts.note: bars are measures of music, not pubs

explanation.surface: A writer who works in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music sets down notes in measures called bars.

clue.text: They use first impressions to eradicate wrong types

definitions.text: They use first impressions to eradicate wrong types

parts.words: They use first impressions to eradicate wrong types
parts.note: first impressions are printers' trial copies, and wrong types are misprinted characters to be corrected

explanation.surface: People who judge others on first sight to get rid of unsuitable characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkers of printed galleys mark typesetting errors on early printed copies before publication.

clue.text: A child of the pen

parts.note: a pen is a female swan, so her offspring is meant, not a writer's brainchild

explanation.surface: A literary work as the offspring of its author.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan; the female swan is called a pen.

clue.text: Loan shark employer admits game being up

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the employer word holds the game inside it

parts.note: a user is one who employs something

indicators.note: being up in a down clue means the game is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A loan shark's boss lets on that the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant interest, exactly what a loan shark is.

clue.text: Point to agent in sight

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone directs a secret agent who has come into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to spot it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: They may be eaten in Morocco, inviting glances

definitions.text: They may be eaten in Morocco
definitions.meaning: ovine eyeballs are a delicacy in some North African cooking
amorous, longing looks cast at someone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means amorous looks, and literally names a dish of ovine eyeballs.

clue.text: Result in directions being put to wrong use

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of use are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Instructions misapplied lead to a bad outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence, a verb synonym of result.

clue.text: Very impressed, we put in small announcement

indicators.note: put in means the pronoun goes inside the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is a small advertisement
taken as written

explanation.surface: We were thrilled to place a classified ad.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with wonder and reverence, that is, deeply impressed.

clue.text: They are utterly conclusive

parts.note: utterly is read as by uttering: the final things said, especially by a dying person

explanation.surface: Statements that settle a matter completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Final utterances before death, or the closing remark in an argument that ends it.

clue.text: He has to be what he is

definitions.text: He has to be what he is

parts.words: He has to be what he is
parts.note: a person is defined by having things: possession makes him the possessor

explanation.surface: A man must simply accept his own nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is one who has something; without having, he would not be one.

clue.text: Laughs at what could be desired

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of desired might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone mocks what might otherwise be wished for.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or scoff at someone means laughing at them with contempt.

clue.text: Sort of safe seat high-flier appreciates in difficulty

definitions.text: Sort of safe seat high-flier appreciates in difficulty

parts.words: Sort of safe seat high-flier appreciates in difficulty
parts.note: a safe seat suggests politics, but it is an aircraft seat that fires a pilot clear in an emergency

explanation.surface: An ambitious politician is glad of a secure constituency when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: A safe seat is a UK constituency a party is sure to win, and a high-flier an ambitious politician; really it is a pilot bailing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot in trouble is saved by this kind of seat, which catapults him out of the cockpit.
